title: Monic residue relation in a localized monogenic presentation
statement: Let $R$ be a normal Nagata domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] in universe $u$, $K$ its fraction field in universe $v$, $x\in K$, $S=R[x]$, and $m$ a maximal ideal of $S$. There exist $s\in S\setminus m$, a normal Nagata domain $A$ and fraction field $L$, both in universe $\max(u,v)$, $y\in L$, an isomorphism $e:S_s\simeq A[y]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and a monic polynomial $f\in A[X]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] of positive degree such that $f(y)$ belongs to the extension of $m$ along $S\to S_s\xrightarrow{e}A[y]$. No splitting condition is imposed.

proof.text: Obtain a positive-degree p with p(x) in m and leading coefficient a outside m. Then a is nonzero. Apply the compatible principal localization model to a.

Map p by the injective coefficient map c and multiply it by C(u^-1), where u is the unit c(a). leadingCoeff_mul and leadingCoeff_map_of_injective prove monicity; natDegree_C_mul and natDegree_map_eq_of_injective preserve the positive degree. The coefficient and generator equations of e, hom_eval2, and eval2_map identify evaluation of the mapped polynomial with the image of p(x). Ideal.mem_map_of_mem and multiplication by the inverse coefficient prove evaluation membership.
